items.userText:
Build an offline BGP relationship inference and route leak scoring service.
Work in `/workspace`; Python 3.11 and its standard library are available.
Read `PROTOCOL.md` for the complete model, schemas, limits and examples.
Implement `/workspace/submission/main.py` as a standalone Python program.
The evaluator runs `python3 -I /workspace/submission/main.py` in a fresh process.
Read one JSON document from stdin and write one JSON document to stdout.
Normalize AS paths, peel peripheral links and infer core-link probabilities.
Use the specified joint model, then apply declared relationships for scoring.
Return link probabilities, peeling rounds and both path legitimacy scores.
Report the earliest weakest triple and the threshold decision for each query.
Handle reverse links, prepending, IXP removal, loops and empty inputs as specified.
Only `submission/main.py` is collected; keep that directory to this one file.
The file must be regular, singly linked, at most 262144 bytes; no symlinks.
Use only the standard library; the runtime has no network or extra packages.
Evaluation allows one CPU, one process, 1 GiB and 60 CPU seconds per input.
Run `python3 public_check.py` for the public examples; it needs no private files.
The starter implements a prior-only baseline and deliberately fails core inference.
Correctness is assessed on additional bounded networks under this public contract.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The service is complete and fully validated. Summary of the implementation in `/workspace/submission/main.py` (28 KB, single regular file, stdlib only):

**1. Strict intake & validation** — byte bound, UTF-8/JSON well-formedness, duplicate-key detection via `object_pairs_hook`, rejection of floats/`NaN`/`Infinity`/booleans-as-integers, exact key sets, ASN/count/weight/threshold ranges, record-count caps, RIB length sum, query-ID regex & uniqueness, distinct IXPs, unique prior/declaration pairs, and the `order` permutation + induced-width ≤ 4 promise (checked *before* any table allocation or model outcome, so pathological invalid inputs fail in ~25 ms).

**2. Normalization & peeling** — IXP removal then adjacent-duplicate collapse (so prepending merges), loop detection, discarding short/looped RIB records, aggregation of identical directed paths, and simultaneous round-based peripheral marking using the fixed-endpoint rule with pre-round trimming decisions.

**3. Exact joint core inference** — occurrences oriented to traverse `u→v`, predecessor/successor literals with `c2p`/`p2c` endpoint defaults and `2−t` reversal, integer `phi_e` tables over each scope, gcd reduction, bucket elimination along the supplied order, plus an elimination-tree downward pass giving exact integer marginals (with per-component root scaling for disconnected cores). `Z == 0` → `{"error":"zero-partition"}`; a sum-invariant check triggers a naive re-elimination fallback as insurance.

**4. Scoring** — declaration → core marginal → prior → uniform lookup, direction reorientation, exact integer triple minimum/witness/threshold comparison through one common denominator, and a 5-state float DP for `full` (verified against exhaustive enumeration and a closed form).

**Validation performed:** 5/5 public examples; ~700 randomized end-to-end cases against an independently written brute-force reference (cores up to 10 links, multi-round peeling, loops, IXPs, disconnected components); 750+ inference cross-checks against brute force and naive elimination; 4000 randomized exact-scoring comparisons; 74 schema/bounds rejection cases; maximal-input performance (2000 RIB records, 40 000 ASNs, 64 core links, 512 long queries, 4 MiB padded) in ~0.4 s with 200 KB of output.
